We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., direct synthesis from commercially available precursors). Leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <= $405. We don't have price data, but assume typical small molecules are cheap. Need to find a single-step reaction that forms target: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. This looks like a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe a bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-2-en-5-one? Actually structure: methyl 2-oxabicyclo? Let's decode: COC( ... )=O is methyl ester of a carboxylate attached to a bicyclic ring with a ketone. The core is a bicyclo[2.2.2]oct-5-en-2-one? Not sure.

We have template 1914385 from search: It shows product SMILES same as target. Reactant SMILES: [CH2:6]=[CH:7][CH:8]=[CH2:9] (i.e., 1,3-butadiene) plus methyl ester of a cyclohexenone? Actually reactant: CH3O C(=O) C1=CH... Let's parse: "[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1=[CH:10][C:11](=[O:12])[CH2:13]1". That's methyl 2-cyclohexen-1-one? Wait: C5 is attached to carbonyl and part of ring. So reactants: methyl 2-cyclohexen-1-one (or methyl 2-oxocyclohex-2-ene-1-carboxylate) plus 1,3-butadiene. Reaction forms bicyclic product via Diels-Alder (intramolecular?). Actually Diels-Alder between diene and dienophile (the enone). So target can be made by Diels-Alder of methyl 2-cyclohexen-1-one (or methyl 2-oxocyclohex-2-ene-1-carboxylate) with 1,3-butadiene. That is a single step (thermal cycloaddition). Both precursors are commercially available: methyl 2-cyclohexen-1-one? Let's check buyable. Use is_buyable for that SMILES. Need SMILES for methyl 2-cyclohexen-1-one: "COC(=O)C1=CC=CC1"? Not exactly. Actually methyl cyclohex-2-en-1-one-? Wait: The enone is a cyclohexenone with a carbonyl at position 1 and a double bond at 2-3. The methyl ester attached to carbonyl? The SMILES from template: "[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1=[CH:10][C:11](=[O:12])[CH2:13]1". That is methyl 2-oxocyclohex-2-ene-1-carboxylate? Let's generate SMILES: "COC(=O)C1=CC(=O)CC1"? Actually C5 is part of ring, double bond to CH10, carbonyl at C11. So ring: C5 (sp2) double bond to CH10, then C11 carbonyl, then CH2, back to C5. So it's a 5-member? Might be methyl 2-oxocyclohex-2-ene-1-carboxylate (a 6-member ring). Let's approximate SMILES: "COC(=O)C1=CC(=O)CC1". Let's test buyable.
